title: The Hollow Wolf Revisited
premise: Felix Halloran, a mercenary bound by an oath to a god that fell silent twenty years ago, has hidden in the valley of Vell where magic cannot enter—until a child named Wren arrives speaking the First Tongue and bearing a soul-mark that belongs to the court beneath the mountain. Felix learns Wren is the vessel for a soul he himself sold long ago to buy his comrades' lives, and that the Hollow Court has come to collect. To save the child, Felix must leave the valley, cross a land where his broken oath marks him as prey, and steal back the soul from the Court's vault before the winter solstice seals it forever. In the end, Felix offers his own memory-laden soul in exchange; the silent god finally answers—not with power, but with forgiveness—and Felix returns to the valley hollowed of his past yet free at last, raising Wren as the valley's first true magic.
about_author: Juniper Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oaths and folk charms before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse in the northern hills, where they claim the wind still speaks a language older than any kingdom.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Establishes Vell, the godless quiet, and Felix's careful invisibility as a mercenary turned farrier. When a knock comes at night, he finds a child on his doorstep, half-frozen, speaking words no living tongue should know. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in tenderness—the life he built is already ending.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kings
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The child, Wren, cannot be understood by anyone but Felix, whose mercenary years included a season among the First Tongue speakers. He realizes the words are prayers—to his silent god. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past he buried is knocking louder than the child did.

chapters.title: The Mark Beneath the Skin
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Bathing the feverish Wren, Felix finds a soul-sigil burned into the child's back—one he recognizes because it matches the scar over his own heart. He sold something once. He never asked what became of it. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a drowned body.

chapters.title: What the Oath Bought
chapters.summary: POV Felix, with flashback. Twenty years ago, Felix and his company were dying in the mountain passes; he traded a portion of his soul to the Hollow Court to save them—and they died anyway, except him. Emotional beat: bitter arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Grey-cloaked riders appear at the valley's edge—Hollow Court bailiffs who cannot enter but can wait. The village notices. Felix's neighbor Marta covers for him, revealing she has always known more than she said. Emotional beat: belonging tested by suspicion.

chapters.title: Marta's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Marta. Reveals the valley's founding bargain: it exists because someone long ago paid the Court to make it magic-proof—a sanctuary bought with souls, generation after generation. Wren is this cycle's payment. Emotional beat: the horror of inherited debts.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers Forward
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Inside Wren's strange consciousness: fragments of another life, memories of the Court's vaults, knowledge of things not yet happened. Wren knows Felix's name before being told. Emotional beat: eerie innocence carrying an unbearable weight.

chapters.title: Leaving Vell
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Crossing the valley boundary, magic floods back into Felix like cold water—his oath reactivates, marking him visibly to all supernatural eyes. The riders turn to follow. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of becoming visible again.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Gods
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Traveling through countryside dotted with shrines, Felix discovers minor gods still whisper his name—he is infamous, the Wolf Who Broke His Pack. A hedge-priestess offers shelter and warnings about the Court's three gates. Emotional beat: shame worn in public.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Priestess's Price
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The priestess, Sef, agrees to guide them in exchange for one true memory from Felix's past—which she takes and keeps in a glass vial. He chooses which to lose and grieves it immediately. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—memory as currency.

chapters.title: Wolves at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Court hounds catch up at a river crossing; Wren's stolen memories surface and speak the First Tongue aloud, freezing the hounds mid-leap. Wren collapses, more hollowed than before. Emotional beat: protection costing the protected.

chapters.title: The Company of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Felix. At a ruined watchtower, Felix meets the shades of his old comrades—lingering echoes sustained by the soul-portion he sold. They are angry, fragmentary, and they know the way into the mountain. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth—his pack survived as lies he tells himself.

chapters.title: Three Gates Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Sef explains the Court's defenses: the Gate of Names (speak your true name and be owned), the Gate of Debts (pay what you owe or become collateral), the Gate of Silence (where gods cannot follow). Emotional beat: strategic dread; every door costs.

chapters.title: The Gate of Names
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix refuses to give his name and instead gives Wren's false one, buying passage through a technicality—but the Gatekeeper now hunts a child's name across the world. Emotional beat: cleverness as survival, and its moral residue.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Descending into the Hollow Court: a cathedral of bone-white vaults where sold souls flicker like lanterns. Wren recognizes their own soul burning in a case—and reaches toward it involuntarily. Emotional beat: homesickness for a self you've never been.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow Queen
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The Queen reveals the truth: Felix didn't sell his soul for his comrades—he sold Wren's future self, and the Court has grown the child for twenty years as the perfect vessel. She offers Felix a trade: walk away, and keep his memories. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of everything he believed.

chapters.title: The Vault of Sold Things
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Refusing the Queen, Felix breaks into the vault with his ghost-comrades' help; each shade spends itself breaking a ward, dissolving gratefully into peace. He shatters Wren's case—but the solstice bell begins to ring. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Gate of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Fleeing upward with the freed soul-light, Wren and Felix reach the final gate, where the Queen waits. She demands the debt be paid in full: a soul for a soul. Emotional beat: cornered stillness before the leap.

chapters.title: What Felix Offers
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix offers everything—all his memories, his name, his twenty years of penance—as payment. As the Court consumes him, the silent god speaks at last, not in thunder but in a single word of release that unbinds the original contract. Emotional beat: climax—faith answered too late and exactly on time.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of the Court
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The god's word unravels the Court's oldest bargains; the valley's founding debt voids, the Queen crumbles into the first honest silence, and freed souls rise like embers. Wren carries the unconscious Felix toward daylight. Emotional beat: awe—systems built on souls failing all at once.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Hollowed
chapters.summary: POV Marta. Felix returns to Vell with no memories of his past, only instincts and kindness intact. Marta tells him who he was; he decides he'd rather be who he is. Magic, unbound from the old bargain, seeps gently into the valley. Emotional beat: bittersweet rebirth.

chapters.title: The First Tongue, Spoken Softly
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Epilogue a year later: Wren teaches Felix the prayers he once knew, and the valley's children learn them too. The god answers sometimes now—in small ways, to small voices. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging rebuilt not on secrets, but on shared remembering.
